# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(curves:)` (GR-12, the hue curves GR-32; a
  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is
  `QualifierProps.swift`'s `ColorQualifierPatch`, beside `ColorQualifier` (its
  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`
  (`blurred`, set only by `drawAdjustment`) and the pick's `QualifierSample`
  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.
  The `dictionary` extensions on the property types are
  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).
  The graphics engine's wrappers are here too: `GraphicLibrary` (`addFont`,
  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and
  `GraphicModule` (`compile`, `describeJSON`, `svg`; it holds its library
  strongly); their values `GraphicDiagnostic` (with `.error`, `.noModule`
  and `.of(_:)`, the one spelling of a diagnostic made from a message, a
  missing module or a thrown error), `GraphicFailure` (what a
  `diag_out` failure throws; `err_out` stays `ReelCoreError`) and
  `GraphicRaster` are `CoreValues.swift`'s, with `GraphicUsage`, the byte
  bridges `withByteBuffer` and `withMutableByteBuffer` (G-46's toll; never
  `UnsafeMutablePointer(mutating:)`), `SpeedLimits` (a pure move,
  clean-up batch 2), `ReelCoreError` and `Fps.ffiPair` (G6 phase 5's toll), and
  `CoreJSON` (`value`, `snapTicks`: `clipState`'s and `snapCandidates`' JSON
  halves, clean-up round 3's toll; `array`, `overrides`, C1's tolls; `ExportSize.list`,
  `ExportSettings.decoded`, `ReelAV1.Config.decoded`, `withNonNullBytes`, codec-export C5's
  toll), and C1's
  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s
  `ReelAV1`, whose `rc_av1_*` calls stay there), `GraphicDiagnostic.list(json:)`,
  `GraphicFailure.checkSides`, `SpeedLimits.decoded` and the free `withBytes`.
  `MediaDescriptor`, `MediaOriginal`, `mediaURL(for:)`, `originalURL(for:)`,
  `revealURL(for:)` (the original, else the copy), `isTrashed` and
  `bookmarkString(for:)` are `MediaDescriptor.swift`'s: a `media[]` element
  minus its id, and the media-file resolvers; they call no `rc_*`.
  It is also where the op table is read BACK: `ReelOp.coreNames()` over
  `rc_op_names`, and `ReelOp.coreSchemas()` over `rc_op_schemas` — every
  op's ARGUMENTS as JSON Schema, keyed by op name, which
  `AgentCatalog.opTool` prints for all sixty-four op tools.
  `deinit` frees the Rust allocation. It also holds **the one read of
  `rc_project_apply`'s TWO message channels**, in the header's own order — a
  sentence is a refusal, an error message is invalid input, neither written
  is an identity — answered as the `ReelEdit` below.
- `OpDictionaries.swift` — the `dictionary` extensions on the §5.2
  property types (`CropInsets` … `Gradient`), the model's own key names; a
  pure move out of `ReelCore.swift` (#190, issue batch B52b; road map 14's
  MC2 made the same move as `PropsDictionaries.swift`, and the merge kept
  main's file). With
  `ReelCore.swift` and `ReelOps.swift`, the only files that write an op
  argument. `putNullable` is the one writer of a three-state (`T??`)
  patch key: absent, an explicit null, or the value.
- `ReelOps.swift` — `OpArgs`, `ReelOp` and one typed factory per row of
  `core/src/edit.rs`'s op table, plus a RAW factory beside the typed one at
  each door that takes a CALLER's own object — ELEVEN of them (`setVideoRaw`,
  `setAudioRaw`, `setTextRaw`, `setShapeRaw`, `setClipRaw`,
  `setActionEndRaw`, `addTextClipRaw`, `addShapeClipRaw`, `setCanvasRaw`,
  `addBackgroundRaw`, `addZoomActionRaw`), which takes the
  caller's own object as `Any` — never `[String: Any]`, so a non-object is
  refused by the CORE in the words that name the group — and forwards it;
  there is no untyped op-JSON call site anywhere else. Where only ONE
  argument is the caller's (a colour, a region, a new clip's patch) the typed
  factory DELEGATES to the raw one, mapping its optional explicitly, because
  an `Optional<T>.none` widened to `Any?` is a non-nil `Any` wrapping a nil.
  The typed `setActionEnd` LIFTS every top-level null out of its patch into
  `off` (spec §11 CI-14: a typed `.some(nil)` is a switch turned OFF, kept
  at the end), and a null slot inside `audio.eq` into `audio.eq.<slot>`
  (AU-88); `setActionEndRaw`'s nulls stay removals, which is what
  `clearOps` and every agent call send, and it writes `off` only when non-empty and `schema` only when non-nil
  (the agent door fills it for a graphic end from the module's current
  revision, spec §11 G-34).
  `addZoomActionRaw`'s region is `Any` and not `Any?`: an absent key and an
  explicit null are opposite intentions there, and only the tool can tell
  them apart.
  `scope` is a member folded into `json`; `documentLevelNames` MIRRORS
  `scope.rs`'s `refused_inside` (eight names) so one edit can mix a
  document-level op with scoped ones. A table, with
  `edit.rs`'s size exemption.
- `ReelOpSchema.swift` — what an op TAKES, mirroring what
  `core/src/op_schema.rs` publishes: the `properties` and `required` of one
  op's arguments, which are the two things `AgentServer.tool` takes, and
  `table(from:)`, which reads `rc_op_schemas`' JSON into them (SR4-0's pure
  move out of `ReelCore.swift`, whose `coreSchemas()` keeps the call). Here
  rather than next door for `ReelEdit.swift`'s reason — it names no `rc_*`
  symbol — and `properties` stays `[String: Any]` because a Swift type per
  kind would be another spelling of the table.
- `ReelEdit.swift` — what an op ANSWERS, mirroring `core/src/outcome.rs`:
  `ReelEdit` (`.applied` / `.identity` / `.refused`), `ReelRefusal` (the op
  the core declined and the rule's own sentence, carried verbatim), and the
  fold that applies a LIST — which names no `rc_*` symbol, so it lives here
  and not next door. **Only `.applied` is an undo step**; the other two are
  both "the project did not change" and differ only in what a caller can
  SAY. `.project` is the spelling for a caller that treats a refusal as
  nothing happened (a probe, a live drag), and there is one on
  `ReelEdit?` too for the `try?` probes. In the fold **a refusal does not
  stop the list** — a later op still runs after one, exactly as after an
  identity — and the FIRST refusal is answered only when nothing applied.
- `ProjectSnapshot.swift` · `TextProps.swift` · `MotionProps.swift` ·
  `WordProps.swift` · `MediaSnapshot.swift` · `ActionSnapshot.swift` · `ShapeProps.swift` · `CompositionPlan.swift` · `GradeProps.swift` · `CurveProps.swift` · `AudioProps.swift` — the `Codable`, READ-ONLY mirror
  of spec §5.2 every view draws from. READ-ONLY means never written back as
  is: the stored properties are `var`, so a writer edits a COPY
  (`var s = current(); s.blur = v`) rather than rebuilding one through the
  defaulted memberwise initialiser, which silently drops a field it does not
  spell out; `MotionProps.with(_:)` is motion's per-slot copy (#357). `CompositionPlan.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading GR1) is the plan's Swift side (spec §7.2): `PlanSegment`,
  `PlanRamp`, `PlanTrack`, `PlanInstruction` and `CompositionPlan`; `PlanSpeedRamp.source` is
  its `map` as a `SourceMap`, checked once at decode and not a coding key (SR-20 (c)); `PlanDuck`
  and `ducks` are a speech ducker's own multiplier (format 29, spec §11 AU-113). `AudioProps.swift`
  (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, road map "audio" AP11's toll) holds the audio group:
  `AudioProps`, `DuckProps` and `CompressorProps`, with format 29's `DuckMode`,
  `DuckProps.mode` / `preRoll` / `hold` and `FadeShape` (and the popups' titles), and format
  30's `LimiterProps` (`audio.limiter`, spec §11 AU-21) with its patch body,
  and format 31's `AudioProps.isolation` (AU-50), and format 32's `eq`, `hum` and `channels`
  (`AudioEQProps.swift`, AU-31, AU-33, AU-34), and format 33's `gate` and `deEsser`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-43, AU-45), and format 34's `voice`
  (`VoiceProps.swift`, AU-140), and format 37's `leveller`
  (`AudioDynamicsProps.swift`, AU-66);
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`'s `TransitionSnapshot.audioShape` is `plus_3db` when absent, and
  `MediaSnapshot.speech` the media's saved spans. `ShapeProps.swift` (a pure
  move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading L3) holds the shape group: `StrokeProps`,
  `GradientStop`, `Gradient` and `ShapeProps`. `GradeProps.swift` holds `ColorAdjust` (a pure move out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) beside grading's other value types. `ActionSnapshot.swift` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, B87) holds `ActionPatch`, `ActionSnapshot` and `ActionGraphicPatch` — an
  end's `graphic.props` and `kinds`, whose `dictionary` sends `props` only. `MediaSnapshot` (a pure move out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`) carries a copy's or an ffmpeg conversion's `original`, and its `name` is
  the one display-name spelling: the original's name when one is recorded. **Its enums decode LENIENTLY**
  — a misspelt kind becomes the first case, a `T??` field a clear — which is
  why a caller-authored object is never decoded through them (below). The
  one exception is `ClipSource`: an unknown `source.kind` THROWS, and
  `ReelProject.snapshot` then falls back to `.empty`, so the WHOLE project
  draws empty with no error. A new source kind in the core is therefore a
  `ClipSource` case in the same phase (road map 10's G2a added `graphic`): no
  agent handler reads a caller-authored OBJECT at all. A scalar enum
  argument is a different thing and several handlers still parse one by name
  (`enumArg` for `add_zoom_action`'s `fit` or an action's `curve`,
  `set_transition`'s `kind` by hand): the
  core refuses those too, and what this rule forbids is decoding a caller's
  object through a lenient type.
  `MotionProps.dictionary` always writes all three keys, `NSNull` for a nil
  slot, because a core patch of `motion` deep-merges — it is the
  APP's writer saying all three slots, not a replace rule, and it is the only
  edge that writes a whole motion. `MotionEdge` also supplies nonpersisted
  zero-duration activity and inactive display/menu titles (E2-27).
  `TextProps.swift` is the text group and `RecipeReveal` (with format version
  9's `textCase` / `words` / `wordStyle`, the recipe's `word` / `wordPop` and,
  since format version 12, `wordGlide` / `wordFill` / `wordDim`), a pure move
  out of `ProjectSnapshot.swift` because a stored property cannot be added
  from an extension. `RecipeReveal` reads and writes its OWN keys — siblings of
  `hash` and `text` in the `text` source — through `init(siblingsOf:)` and
  `encodeSiblings(to:)`, so a new recipe key costs `FrameRecipe.swift`
  nothing; a key spelled other than the snake-case converter spells it
  decodes silently to that key's default (the amount to 1, the rest to nil).
  `ProjectSnapshot+Graphic.swift` mirrors
  `model_graphic.rs`'s `GraphicProps` as `GraphicSnapshot` (`in` is
  `sourceIn`) and `GraphicPropValue` (string, number, bool; anything else
  `.null`), decoded into `ClipSnapshot.graphic`; `props` keys keep the
  module's own spelling (snake-case conversion does not reach a dictionary's
  keys). `WordProps.swift` mirrors `model_words.rs`
  (`TextCase`, `TextWord`, `WordMode`, `ActivePill`, `WordStyle`)
  — `WordStyle.dictionary` writes ALL eight keys (`active_fill` and `pause_dim` since format version 12; `ActivePill.dictionary` writes `glide`), `NSNull` for a nil slot,
  `MotionProps.dictionary`'s rule, because the core deep-merges
  `word_style` — and holds
  what the renderer and the inspector share: `laidContent` (`case` applied —
  every layout and string index is in ITS UTF-16 space, never `content`'s),
  `tokenCount`, `isUntimedPage`, `TextPatch.contentEdit` and
  `InspectorBinding.contentOps` / `ops(textContent:)` — the Content write,
  decided PER CLIP: `words: []` beside the content in one `set_text` only for
  base clips whose count changed, and never `words` in an action end (W-2,
  W-6). It lives there, not in `InspectorPane.swift`, for the size rule.

**The document.**
- `ProjectDocument.swift` (+`DisplayStem`, +`Recording`, +`SelectedAction`, +`Import`, +`Graphics`, +`GraphicFiles`, +`UndoGroup`, +`CacheSaves`, +`Alerts`)
  — NSDocument, `.framejob` package read/write, and the single mutation
  point (see Undo); `applyEdit`'s `.refused` arm beeps and then posts
  `projectDocumentDidRefuse` with the `ReelRefusal` (spec §11 CI-10), which
  the editor forwards to the inspector's refusal strip. Holds the SIX pieces of view state nothing persists —
  playhead, clip selection, in/out range, `selectedMedia`, `nestPath` and
  `selectedAction` — re-clamped by `clampViewState` in that order with the
  scope FIRST, since the selection clamp measures against whatever
  container the scope left. `selectedAction` (spec §11 CI-1) is nil or one
  action of the SINGLE selected clip; `+SelectedAction` holds its queries,
  its one deliberate writer `selectAction(_:)` (which stores nil for an id
  that is not `singleSelectedClip`'s) and the ENTRY rule
  `syncSelectedAction()`, run from `playhead`'s and `selection`'s `didSet`
  against `lastInsideAction`. The clamp re-reads `lastInsideAction` BEFORE
  its last line writes the playhead, so an edit, undo or redo under a
  stationary playhead never enters a span — keep those two lines above
  that write. `nestPath` is a
  PATH of (nest, clip) steps, not a nest id, because two clips can show one
  nest at two starts; `editedProject` is a STORED, memoised `rc_project_scoped`
  handle, and `project` still means the parent for save, export and
  consolidate. A range is cleared on every scope change: a pair of ticks means
  one thing inside a nest and another to an export. `+UndoGroup`:
  `inUndoGroupIfRegistered` runs a body with an undo group pending, and
  `registerUndo(restoring:actionName:)`'s first statement
  (`openPendingUndoGroup()`) opens it at the body's first registration, at the
  body's level and never while undoing or redoing; a body that registers
  nothing leaves undo and redo untouched (#167); `registerUndo` stays the one
  registrar. `applyEdit(_:_:amending:)` (#272) undoes the step that ended at
  `step` before committing, when `project` is still that handle, so a strip's
  off-knob double-click is one step. `cacheDirectory` calls `packageContentsDidChangeOnDisk()` when it
  creates `cache/` — only if the package's date, read through a fresh `URL`
  before the create, is still `fileModificationDate`, so an outside change made before it is not absorbed — and that method re-reads the date through a fresh
  `URL`, because `fileURL` still holds the date it cached at open (#138).
  `+CacheSaves` is the `save(to:ofType:for:completionHandler:)` override
  every save funnels through, bracketing it with the cache ledger's
  `saveBegan` / `saveEnded` (#115, #169).
  `+Import` is File ▸ Add Media… and every drop into an open project
  (`importMedia`, the probe chain and the one grouped commit), the opening
  read's probe (`probeForOpening`, a cancelled copy as `.userCancelled`), and the Media
  tab's Relink… and the missing-media sheet's body (`relinkMedia(_:)`: each
  file probed through `MediaImporter.probe`, one grouped "Relink Media" edit
  carrying each descriptor as `relink_media`'s `probe`, spec §11 #63, then
  `generateCaches()`; the missing-media sheet's door then alerts each
  unreadable file and each refused sentence (#180) through `present(_:)`).
  `+MissingCopies` re-copies, on open, a WebM/MKV copy that is missing or in
  the Trash from its recorded original (spec §11 #228-O), through
  `MediaImporter.probeBuiltInCopy` (never ffmpeg, never a question); a
  read on main or inside `withoutAsking` (an agent's `open_project`, off
  main since #231) passes no watch.
  `+Alerts` is `present(_:)`: every error the document shows waits in one
  queue (`DocumentAlertQueue`) and shows one alert sheet at a time, each asked
  for a main-queue turn after the last one's `didPresent` or the window's last
  sheet end, and only while no sheet is attached, since AppKit drops an error
  sheet asked for while another is attached (#195, `relink_sheet_probe.py`
  A1–A5); with no window, it is app-modal at once. `+Graphics`
  is the document's side of the package's `graphics/`:
  `startGraphicStore()`, run from `makeWindowControllers()` and seeding an
  untitled document's root from `autosavedContentsFileURL/graphics`, and
  `graphicsWrapper()`, the lazy wrapper the save whitelist carries — for a
  SAVED document it reads `<fileURL>/graphics` itself and never asks the
  store, so a nil store can never drop a saved folder; for an untitled one
  it carries the store's root only when `GraphicStore.holdsContent` (an
  entry, file or directory, that is neither hidden nor the manual) says so
  (spec §11 G-14).
  `startGraphicStore()` also installs the document's compiled set in
  `GraphicRegistry` and observes the store's `.graphicsDidChange`, whose
  handler updates the registry and THEN posts `.projectGraphicsDidChange`
  (object: the document) — never `rescan()` there; `stopGraphicStore()`, from
  `close()`, removes the observer, drops the set, stops the store and removes
  BOTH untitled roots — the graphics root (`removeScratchRoot()`) and
  `temporaryCacheDirectory` (`removeTemporaryCacheDirectory()`); the cache
  root goes at close ONLY, never at the first save, because the timeline and
  any pass in flight still hold its path (G-19 (d)). `startGraphicStore()` also observes the document's own
  `.projectDocumentDidChange` and ends with one `reconcileGraphicNames()`;
  `stopGraphicStore()` removes that observer. `+ConvertedThumbnails`:
  `startCaches()`, from `makeWindowControllers()` in place of
  `generateCaches()`, observes the document's own `.projectDocumentDidChange`
  and starts a cache pass for each media whose converting Camera Log differs

`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

**Playback and rendering.**
- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is

**The core's edge.**

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

# app/CLAUDE.md — Swift app rules

Applies to everything under `app/`. Build/verification commands and the FFI
lockstep are in the root `CLAUDE.md`; the full design is
`designs/spec/` (§3–4 the UI, §7.4–7.8 the platform side; its `README.md` is
the index). The
long form of each entry below — why each file is the shape it is, and the
traps its history turned up — is `designs/adr/app-file-history.md` (the
full history, every size toll and measurement, is archived; see its
"Original" line); this file is what governs a file now. Files
are listed by family; a file with a header comment of its own carries its
detail there.

## File map

**The core's edge.**
- `ReelCore.swift` — the **only** home for `rc_*` calls: `ReelProject`
  (handle + lazily decoded `ProjectSnapshot`; `json`, `snapshot` and
  `planJSON` are memoised PER HANDLE, so keep handles rather than minting
  them; so is `sourceMap(_:)`, `rc_project_source_map` decoded and checked
  once per handle and clip, SR-20), timecode, snapping (export presets/sizes/settings are
  `ExportValues.swift`'s, a pure move, HDR H-1), `ReelSpeed.limits` (the
  core's speed range and audio ceiling, typed as `SpeedLimits` in
  `CoreValues.swift` — no Swift file types a speed bound), `ReelColor` (`rc_normalise_color`, G-25), `ReelGraphicPackage` (`rc_graphic_package_write`, G-46; `read`, `rc_graphic_package_read`, G-47), `GraphicLibrary.usage()` (`rc_graphic_library_usage`) and
  `ReelContainer` (`rc_container_*`, a WebM/Matroska file's index,
  #216-R) and `ReelWebM` (`rc_webm_*`, the `av1_webm` writer, spec §11 CX-15) and `ReelHDR10` (`rc_hdr10_peak`, spec §11 HD-6; `av1Peak`,
  `rc_hdr10_av1_peak`, HD-18; `stillPeak`, `rc_hdr10_still_peak`, HD-20), and `GraphicLibrary.imageCache(limit:)`
  (`rc_graphic_image_cache`, G-39); `ReelCoreError`, `Fps.ffiPair` and `ReelTime`'s
  seconds conversions are `CoreValues.swift`'s (G6 phase 5's toll T2 and speed ramps SR4-0,
  pure moves); the typed patches are `TypedPatches.swift`'s (`VideoPatch`,
  `AudioPatch`, `ClipPatch`, the `ActionPatch` extension; a pure move, B73),
  `TextPatch` (with `case`, `words` and `word_style`) is `TextPatch.swift`'s,
  moved out so it could grow, and `ShapePatch` `ShapePatch.swift`'s (a pure
  move, the toll for `ReelColor`). `VideoPatch.color` is a sparse `ColorPatch`
  (`GradeProps.swift`, which holds `ColorAdjust` (moved out of
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift`, grading-2 G2-0) with its neutrality helpers, and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(tone:)`, and the wheels' `ColorWheel`, `ColorWheels`,
  `ColorWheelPatch`, `ColorWheelsPatch`, `ColorWheelKind` and
  `LayerUniforms.apply(wheels:)` (GR-11)); `VideoPatch.curves` is
  `CurveProps.swift`'s `ColorCurvesPatch`, beside `CurvePoint`,
  `CurveDomain`, `CurveChannel`, `CurveBlend` (a channel blended inside an
  action, spec §11 GR-34; `ColorCurves.blends`, never encoded), `ColorCurves` and

  pure move out of `GradeProps.swift`, grading-4 T4-0); `VideoPatch.qualifier` is

  `blur`, `blursSelection` and `selectionSigma`, GR-35), `QualifierUniforms`

  (GR-13), so a row writes
  only its own key to every selected clip. `word_style` has ONE
  app-side writer, `CaptionLayout.place` (W-10). `ReelAgentSocket` (road map
  14's MC2) wraps `rc_agent_socket_start` / `_release`: `start` throws the
  core's sentence, `release` is the quit's unlink-if-still-ours with no join.

  `OpDictionaries.swift`'s (below).

  `addAsset`, `rasterize`, `families()`; frozen by its first compile,
  rasterize or `families()`) and

  fix-pass moves: `ReelAV1.Config` / `.Color` (an extension of `ReelCore.swift`'s

**Frozen files.** `EditorViewController.swift`, `TimelineView.swift`,
`PreviewCanvasView.swift`, `AgentServer.swift` are **frozen at current
size**: anything adding more than ~50 lines goes in an extension file
(`EditorViewController+<Feature>.swift`, `TimelineView+<Feature>.swift`,
`AgentServer+<Feature>.swift`) or a new `…SheetController`, and the frozen
file keeps only the wiring — a stored property, a closure assignment, a
validator arm, a draw call. The pieces extension files build on are therefore
internal, not private. Pitfalls: a selector declared `@objc` on an extension
needs NO forward in the frozen file (a second declaration is an error); a
command whose body sits at the foot of a non-extension feature file carries
its validator arm there too, or the item falls through to the closing
`return true`; `handleEditorCharacter`'s bare-key `switch` matches in SOURCE
order, so a bare `case "x"` goes BELOW any modified `case "x" where …`; and
`handleEditorKey` refuses while a sheet is attached, because a sheet is
window-modal and the preview panel's forwarded keys would otherwise reach
the key map behind it.

- `Playback.swift` (+`Meter`, +`PreviewQuality`, +`Step`, +`Scope`, +`Prefetch`) — one
  `AVPlayer` over the plan's composition; the transport, JKL, the rate KVO; `+Meter` is the level meter, moved out under
  the size rule; `+Scope` also holds `seekFinished()` and `report(_:)`
  (hdr H-3's pure move). `recompose()` re-colours the player's copy of the
  composition without a rebuild (`previewComposition(…, sdrVersion:)`, the
  way Preview Quality does): View ▸ Show SDR Version, spec §11 HD-14. **Only a seek someone ASKED for reports a time**:
  `seek(to:)` is that door, and Playback's own RESTORES — the rebuild's item
  swap and re-seek, the paused refresh's round trip — go through `startSeek`
  silently and report once, only if they come to rest off the last reported
  tick; a scope change seeks through `seekAfterRebuild(to:)`: its time is the
  NEW container's, so the outgoing item is neither sought nor heard and the
  rebuild in flight lands there, heard once (#130, `scope_playhead_probe.py`);
  an asked seek that arrives while a restore is seeking is heard once, when it
  lands; `update`'s same-plan and empty-plan arms discard a rebuild in flight;
  a held scope change whose rebuild fails, or whose new plan is empty, drops
  the item rather than leave the outgoing one, keeps its time and is heard
  once (`endHoldWithoutItem` in `+Scope`, #185; the seek flags are internal
  for `+Scope` alone); `rebuildHop` is the probe's seam, nil in the app, and
  its block takes an error it delivers as the build's failure; `report(_:)` is the one
  caller of `onTimeChanged`. While paused, an observer callback is heard only
  for the tick the player is at or seeking to, and only when it differs from
  the last report — a late callback for a superseded seek or a swapped-out
  item is dropped (#204, #209; `playhead_echo_probe.py` twice·1, pause·1) —
  and every seek's landing reports its rest once when it differs. `+Step`
  also holds the main hop `onMain`. `+Prefetch` is the playing preview's
  graphics prefetch (spec §11 G-36, #127): `syncPrefetch(from:seeking:)`,
  called from the rate KVO, `startSeek` (with the seek's TARGET, never
  `currentTime`, which still reads the player there) and `update`'s
  same-plan arm while playing, and stopped in `invalidate` and `deinit`;
  `recipeKey` is internal for it. `syncPrefetch` first notes activity for
  Background render, and `startBackgroundRender` (G-38) starts a paused pass
  on the composition's grid (`prefetchGrid`), answering why not
  (`.busy` re-arms the clock, `.notNeeded` waits for the next activity). An echoed restore
  moved the playhead (0 and back on every rebuild), and the timeline reveals
  every moved playhead, so a clip drag yanked the view
  (`playhead_echo_probe.py`). **A paused refresh is a one-tick round trip**
  (`refreshPausedFrame`): a zero-tolerance seek to the current time is a
  NO-OP on macOS 26.5.1, so the refresh seeks one tick off and returns; parked
  at the end it rests on the last frame's final tick, because the end tick
  composes black. Do not put a same-time seek back. Preview Quality overrides
  `renderSize` on a copy of the builder's
  `BuiltComposition.videoConfiguration` here (`Playback.previewComposition`,
  static so `phase8_chrome.py` calls it), keeping the
  canvas's EXACT aspect (`m · (w/g, h/g)`, coarser when the divisor does not
  divide `g`, Full for a coprime canvas); `AVPlayerItem.videoComposition` is
  a COPY property, so the setter re-assigns. `makePreviewLayer` is the one
  door to a second `AVPlayerLayer`.
  The item is dropped only for an EMPTY timeline (`plan.duration <= 0`,
  where the transport beeps). Never gate it on the plan's track lists: a
  timeline of only graphics, text, shapes or images has no plan track and
  plays over the builder's placeholder (road map 10 §10.8,
  `media_less_playback_probe.py`).

- **CJ-13 — The startup parity check gains a sixth part: every keyed tool exists, and its
  catalog description says it needs its key.** In `AgentServer+Parity.swift`; root `CLAUDE.md`'s
  "FIVE parts" becomes six.

**CJ2a's and CJ2b's block (the analysis lane).**

- **CJ-20 — Analysis is a cache, made on demand.** It never runs at import, is never project
  state, and is never read by the composition plan or the frame recipe. A planner reads it and
  writes ordinary edits. A render drawn from it (CO's masks) is substituted by Swift, as a
  reversed file is (§5.6). So no analysis kind bumps the format.
- **CJ-21 — One lane, `AnalysisLane`, process-wide, apart from the import lane.** Width 1 unless
  spike CJ-S3 earns 2; `.utility`; its own queue, never the cooperative pool and never
  `MediaCacheLane`. Jobs are wanted by owners — a document's command, a tool call, an export — as
  ramp audio's renders are (SR-12): a job nobody wants is cancelled, one wanted again while it
  runs is not, and `wait` returns on landing, failure or cancellation.
- **CJ-22 — The store.** `cache/analysis/<kind>/<media id>.json` (plus a payload file where a
  kind needs one), one per media and kind, holding RUNS over source spans in media source ticks:
  a hit is a stored run containing the asked span, a miss runs exactly that span, and the store
  drops the runs the new one contains (TR-14's shape). Written only through
  `CacheLedger.publish`, sorted keys, `.atomic`. The marker is an `AnalysisStamp`: the source's
  identity (`CacheStamp`'s size, modified second and duration; no path), the kind and its version,
  a digest of the kind's parameters, the OS build and the compute device. Any other stamp is a
  miss and the next store replaces the file whole. Coordinates are normalised 0…1 in the media's
  display orientation, origin top-left; times are media source ticks, so any clip, speed, ramp or
  reversal over the file reuses them through `SourceMap` and `ReverseMirror`.
- **CJ-23 — The frame reader.** A kind asks for frames at its own size and rate, in display
  orientation. A media whose picture converts at step 0 (Camera Log, HLG, PQ) is read through the
  thumbnails' converted path, so analysis sees what the person sees; every other media through a
  scaled `AVAssetReader`. CJ-S3 may move the line.
- **CJ-24 — `shots`, the first kind: hard cuts from a deterministic picture difference, no ML.**
  Each frame at the media's own rate, read at a long side of 256 px, is reduced to a joint
  colour histogram; a cut is a frame whose distance to the previous one passes the threshold and
  which is at least the minimum shot length after the last cut. The threshold, the minimum and
  the dissolve rule are fixed in CJ2a against the synthetic fixture before the proof's run.
- **CJ-25 — `get_media_analysis {media, kind, from?, to?}` reads any kind, running or reusing it,
  and answers the window's results in source ticks with `cached` and the stamp.** It waits with
  a bound, as `get_transcript` does, and is `get_transcript`'s counterpart for pictures and
  sounds. Answers are windowed and capped by size, the cap and the over-cap refusal fixed in CJ2a.
- **CJ-26 — A canned analysis is honoured only for a proof.** A marker with `"canned": true`
  carries only the source identity, and is read only in a build with `FRAMEJOB_DEV_TOOLS` launched
  with `-RCDevAnalysisCanned YES`, so a planner's proof is byte-exact on any Mac and
  Distribution never reads one.

  shows it: the command's name, each media's progress, Stop. Stop withdraws the command's wants
  and lands nothing. A tool call shows no sheet and waits.
- **CJ-28 — Clip ▸ Split at Shot Changes and `split_at_shots {clips?}` (CJ2b).** The selected
  media clips (else none: the item validates off) are split at each cut inside their played
  window, mapped to clip time through the source map, on the canvas grid, as one undo step "Split
  at Shot Changes". A cut within one frame of a clip's edge is dropped. Locked tracks and linked
  partners follow `split`'s own rules (AU-92). Over the clip ceiling, the whole command is
  refused before any split, naming how many splits it needed and how many fit.

**CJ3's block (faces).**

- **CJ-30 — `faces`, the first machine-learning kind, for VR and SW.** Per sample: each face's
  rectangle, confidence, roll and yaw (`VNDetectFaceRectanglesRequest`), and its mouth opening
  (`VNDetectFaceLandmarksRequest`: the inner-lip gap over the face's height), at request
  revisions pinned in the kind's version. Samples are 10 a second of source and frames are read at
  a long side of 1280 unless CJ-S2's verdict says otherwise.
- **CJ-31 — Identity is linked, not recognised.** A face keeps its id from one sample to the next
  when their rectangles overlap by intersection-over-union ≥ 0.3, and across a gap of at most 1 s;
  ids restart at a `shots` cut when that kind is cached. No face is ever named or compared across
  media. Values are stored raw: smoothing is a planner's.
- **CJ-32 — The compute device is pinned and in the stamp.** The Neural Engine when the Mac has
  one, else the GPU, unless CJ-S2's verdict picks otherwise; a proof compares against the cache,
  never against a recomputation (E9's rule).

**CJ4's block (source ranges).**

- **CJ-40 — `add_clip`, `insert_clip` and `overwrite_clip` take an optional `source_in` (media
  source ticks, default 0) and an optional `duration` (timeline ticks, default the rest of the
  file from `source_in`).** `source_in` is snapped to the canvas grid, as a front trim from 0
  would place the in point. Refused, each in its own sentence: `source_in` below 0 or at or past
  the file's last frame; either argument on a still or an image media ("a still has no source
  window"); a `duration` longer than the window, naming the longest that fits
  (`source_window.rs`'s `longest_duration_on_grid_of`). A `duration` of 0 or less is invalid
  input. `insert_clip` shifts by the placed duration. No format change: the stored clip is the
  one a placement and two trims make today.

  locked or not, by `split_clip`'s rules; clips wholly outside go; a transition with a partner
  outside goes with it; markers inside stay and shift, the others go; nests stay only when a kept
  clip shows them; `next_id` and every kept id are unchanged, so per-media caches stay keyed.

  Document-level: refused inside a nest scope. It has its op tool, as every op does.
- **CJ-51 — File ▸ New Project from Range… (New Project from Timeline when no In–Out range is
  set) and `new_project_from_range {from?, to?, path?}`.** The current project is not changed and
  no undo step is made in it. A new untitled document takes `keep_range` with

### Spikes

Each rule is fixed here, before its run. Instruments go in `tools/proof/creator_spike/`; each
run's `results.json` stores the SHA-256 of `creator-jobs.md` as `rule_sha256` (CAM-2's
precedent), and the verdict is recorded in the road map and in the decision named.

- **CJ-S1 — The clip ceiling (at CJ0; decides CJ-9).** Question: how many clips can a project
  hold before editing, planning, drawing or undo stop being usable? Projects of N = 4,096, 8,192,
  16,384 and 32,768 one-second media clips over four tracks of one media, generated as packages.
  Measured: (1) `rc_project_apply` of `split` at the middle, median of 20; (2) `rc_project_from_json`
  plus `rc_composition_plan`; (3) `frame_recipe` at 20 random times, median; (4) in the Release app
  over MCP, one `ripple_delete_ranges` of 100 ranges and its undo; (5) the app's resident memory
  after 50 undo steps of `split`. N above 4,096 needs the bench to raise the cap in a scratch
  build only. **Rule:** N_max is the largest N for which (1) ≤ 50 ms, (2) ≤ 500 ms, (3) ≤ 2 ms,
  (4) applies in ≤ 1 s and undoes in ≤ 1 s, and (5) grows by at most a sixteenth of physical
  memory. N_max > 4,096 → CJ6 raises the ceiling to N_max; otherwise CJ-9 keeps 4,096.
- **CJ-S2 — Vision faces on this Mac (at CJ0 when S-TH1 exists, else at CJ3's start; decides
  CJ-30 and CJ-32).** Question: are face tracks deterministic, fast and found on the owner's
  material, and on which device and at what size? Inputs: S-TH1, S-TH2 (V-Log), a portrait iPhone
  file, and the moving-still fixture. Measured: (1) the cache bytes over three runs on each of
  CPU, GPU and Neural Engine; (2) the largest rectangle difference between devices; (3) seconds
  per minute of source at 10 samples a second, frames at long side 720, 1080 and 1440, faces
  alone and with landmarks; (4) the share of samples with a face over S-TH1's first 60 s, which
  its recording brief makes front-facing; (5) on S-TH2, that share on the raw log picture and on
  the converted one; (6) peak memory. **Rules:** the device is the fastest whose three runs are

- **W-7 — Pages are filled to a MEASURED width, in one Swift builder, and
  the cue builder does not change** (road map 8 §4 W-7, §5c; built by W4a,
  §10.9). `CaptionPages` fills each page greedily by
  `LayerRenderers.measuredSize` of the page as it will be placed — face,
  size, case, outline and word-style headroom — against 0.86 of the canvas
  width; a page wraps only when a lone word does not fit even at 80 % of its
  size, and Karaoke pages to two lines by design. `CaptionCues` keeps its
  five rules and Subtitles output is byte-identical. **Pauses are word gaps
  of 0.25 s or more plus sentence punctuation**: `SilenceDetector` and
  `MediaSpeech` are not consulted, because the pager is pure and
  `Transcriber.transcribe` has no cache directory to ask (W4a measured the
  pangram's two pauses breaking by punctuation alone). **Each engine's
  `lead` lives in `CaptionPages.lead(for:)`** — on-device +270 ms,
  AssemblyAI −60 ms — applied once in its normalisation and never in
  `CaptionCues`. **A page is confined to its job's span** `[start, start +
  duration)` (`Transcriber.Job.span`): `lead` and `hold` never carry a page
  past its clip, a word pushed off the end sits on the clip's last frame

content.content:
- **SW-75 — Detach Audio on a file with several audio tracks makes one sound clip per track**,
  the picture's sound off, all in one group, each on its own new track below, one undo step; the
  menu item reads "Detach Audio Tracks" there. Clip ▸ Detach Audio Channels makes one mono clip
  per channel of the clip's stream. `detach_audio {clip, per?: "track"|"channel"}`; absent is
  "track", which on a one-track file is today's Detach Audio exactly.

**SW8 — one-microphone shows.**
- **SW-80 — Faces are read by Vision's face landmarks**, `VNDetectFaceLandmarksRequest` at
  revision 3 with the 76-point constellation (its `innerLips` and `outerLips`), ten samples a
  second per angle, into the shared video-analysis cache (CJ shared need). No model is bundled.
- **SW-81 — Mouth activity.** Per angle, its largest tracked face's inner-lip opening over its
  mouth width; activity is that ratio's standard deviation over 0.5 s. With one microphone, a
  step is speech when the microphone's voice ≥ 0.5; the speaker is the angle whose activity is
  highest when it is at least 1.5× the next and above a floor set by SW-S3; otherwise the step is
  crosstalk. SW-22's shot rules follow unchanged.
- **SW-82 — How sure it says it is**, by SW-S3's band: in the middle band the sheet reads "Faces
  guess who is talking; check the cuts" and `min_shot` defaults to 3 s.

**SW9a — angles and the Angle Viewer.**
- **SW-90 — Angles are derived, not stored.** A shot's angles are SW-13's candidates. The
  program track is the selected clip's track, else the front track with a media clip at the
  playhead. No format change. (Persisting `tracks[].angles` is the alternative, asked at SW9a.)
- **SW-91 — The viewer is a tap on the compositor.** While View ▸ Angle Viewer is shown, the
  plan includes the angle tracks' video even when hidden (an option the core takes, not a
  persisted field), the recipe keeps them off the canvas, and the compositor draws each angle's
  frame into its cell of a grid texture handed to the viewer, as `WaveformTaps` are handed
  `ProjectSnapshot.swift` (1,454) take rows from every bet; the tolls land in CJ0.

### Not in this bet

Lifted non-goals that this bet does not build, and why, each to be filed as a candidate issue
when the road map closes:

content.content:
### 3. Make Vertical Version

**Pitch.** File ▸ Make Vertical Version… writes a 9:16 or 1:1 version of a finished 16:9 edit. Each clip fills the frame and follows the face, person or salient region that Vision found on the Mac. It does this with ordinary eased x, y and scale actions the creator can nudge. In a screen recording made after bet 2, it follows the cursor instead. Captions re-lay for the short side, and graphics re-layout from the canvas size. A shot that cannot be cropped gets Add Blurred Background.

**Why it puts Frame Job ahead.** Subject-tracking reframe is table stakes. OpusClip [C11], CapCut [C4], Premiere [P21], Final Cut Pro for iPad [P17], Riverside [C9], Kapwing [C20] and Screen Studio [S1] all ship it, and auto-repurposing is the most-wanted creator AI feature in one survey [D2]. Frame Job pulls ahead on terms. CapCut moved Auto Reframe behind Pro in April 2026 [C4]. Here it is free and local, and the result is editable pan actions rather than a render. If the owner chooses linked versions (one cut, with a framing per shape), Frame Job is ahead of every rival, because their vertical copies drift from the master.

**Builds on.** `fill_scale` (`edit_fit.rs`); Add Blurred Background (`edit_background.rs`); word captions sized to the shorter side (`CaptionStyle.swift`); graphics that read `ctx.canvas`; actions (`edit_action.rs`); nests (`edit_nest.rs`); `set_canvas` (`edit_canvas.rs`); File ▸ Duplicate; the E9 Vision spike in `tools/proof/effects_spike/`.

**Effort.** M as a regenerated copy. L for linked versions, which need a canvas per version, framing overrides per clip and a format bump.

**Risks and what comes first.**
- Spec §1 lists auto-reframe as a non-goal, so a §11 decision must lift it first. The reason given there, heavy pixel work outside the one-pass compositor, no longer applies: the analysis runs offline and its output is actions.
- No two actions on one clip may overlap, of any kind. A clip that already carries an action (a zoom, a grade, a ramp) needs a wrapping nest, and a nest's canvas freezes at the size it was nested at.
- `set_canvas` does not rescale action end states. A screencast's existing zoom actions keep their 16:9 targets, and the planner must rewrite them.
- `MediaCacheLane` is a width-2 lane for audio decodes, so video analysis needs its own lane, cache kind and ledger rows.
- The planner should use face, human and saliency rectangles with tracking, not masks: the E9 spike found that foreground masks flicker on video.
- Two people in frame, a speaker leaving the frame, and shot changes inside one flattened clip each need a rule.

## Decisions for the owner

1. **Lead segment.** Recommendation: creators who record themselves talking, meaning talking-head YouTube and screen tutorials (bets 1, 2 and 6). Then repurposing to shorts (bets 3 and 4), then video podcasts (bet 5).
2. **Which spec §1 non-goals to lift, and how far.**
   - Auto-reframe: needed for bet 3.
   - Multicam: narrowly, as speaker switching on stacked tracks, or fully, as a multicam clip with an angle grid (bet 5).
   - ML and heavy pixel work: needed for camera cutout (issue #124's D5, bet 6).
   - Optical-flow retiming and motion blur: stay out until a spike.
   - A plugin system: stays out.
3. **Which spec §11 decisions to amend before code.**
   - TR-3, AI-6 and W-9, so that a deterministic retake pass may strike words (bet 1).
   - `recording.md`: cursor as data, callouts, a source kind and a schema bump (bet 2).
   - AI-10, for Proposals.
   - W-10, for inspector caption styling.
4. **Shortcut capture.** Whether the recorder may ask for the Input Monitoring grant, with capture opt-in and limited to modifier shortcuts by default.
5. **Vertical versions.** A regenerated copy (M), or linked versions in one project, where one cut has a framing per shape (L, with a format bump).
6. **Language models.** Claude on the creator's key only, or Apple FoundationModels as a no-key fallback. FoundationModels needs Apple Intelligence on and has a context of about 4k tokens.
7. **Cloud.** Confirm that bring-your-own key stays the only cloud model. Then either accept that filler detection stays AssemblyAI-only (TR-7), or fund an on-device filler pass.
8. **Performance.** Allow one measurement of multi-stream 4K and multi-hour playback now, despite the features-first order, before bet 5 and before any claim to lead. Add proxies only if the measurement falls short.
9. **Real use.** Cut at least one real video per lead segment in Frame Job before or alongside the first bet, so the bets are tested against real work.
10. **Positioning.** Whether to present Frame Job to creators as free, open, on-device and credit-free. That position answers the most common switching triggers: price rises [C5] [S7] [D19], metered credits [D7] [P7] and content-licence scares [D18].

pipeline (design → adversary → implement → review → fix), built in a lane of its own, gated
  (`make gate`) and committed there, then rebased onto the integration branch one at a time by
  one serialized integrator and gated again. At most three lanes. A lane whose next phase needs
  another lane's unlanded phase waits; it never builds against an unlanded one. Format versions
  are provisional from 38: when another lane landed a bump first, the integrator renumbers the
  bump, its `schema_vN.rs` and its `format_history.rs` paragraph. Merging into main follows CJ0's
  question 1.
- **CJ-7 — IDs and records.** Phases are `XXn` with XX in TX, CU, VR, FC, SW, CO and CJ; a phase
  split by size is `XXna`, `XXnb`, sharing its block. Phase XXn's decisions are XX-n0…XX-n9
  (XX0's are XX-1…XX-9). Spikes are XX-S1, XX-S2…, each with its rule fixed and stored by SHA-256
  before its run (CAM-2's precedent). Manual checks are `JOB-n`, numbered by the integrator at
  landing. Handoffs are `~/.claude/litecode/framejob/cj-<phase id lowercased>`. The road map,
  `designs/creator-jobs.md`, holds each phase's record.
- **CJ-8 — Shared reservations, so lanes do not collide.** (a) The fifth inspector tab is TX's
  Transcript; another tab, or a panel beside the inspector, needs a decision of its own, because
  `InspectorViewController.swift` is frozen and five titles at the 280 pt minimum are 56 pt each.
  (b) The layer pass's `texture(4)` is CO's layer mask; `texture(5)` is CU's cursor sprite if CU
  draws the cursor in the layer pass. `LayerUniforms` groups of four are appended in landing
  order. (c) Every analysis kind lives under `cache/analysis/<kind>/` (CJ2a); no bet adds a
  sibling folder for analysis. (d) The road map's tools join dispatch through one table,
  `AgentServer+CreatorJobs.swift`'s `creatorHandlers`, merged into the frozen file's by one line
  (CJ0's toll T8). (e) A bet that adds a key equivalent records it, and the integrator checks
  `docs/guide/menus-and-shortcuts.md` for a clash before landing. (f) A bet's command is a
  composite over ops landing as one undo step through `performGroupedEdit`, and its tool runs the
  same planner (SY-1's shape), unless its rule must hold inside the core, in which case it is an

objections.where: How it fits the tree, 'Caches and lanes' (vr.md:114-141); VR-10..VR-17; VR1 section (vr.md:519-575); VR-S1, VR-S2; phase table 'Depends on CJ1'; VR6's landmarks (VR-60)
objections.claim: VR builds its own copy of the analysis infrastructure that the CJ section already owns. It also calls that infrastructure 'CJ1', but in cj.md CJ1 is the key gate. The result is two lanes, two cache layouts, two shot detectors, two face passes, two tools, two sheets and two device rules.
objections.evidence: cj.md: CJ1 = 'the key gate' (cj.md:515, 632). The analysis lane and store are CJ2a (CJ-21, CJ-22, `AnalysisLane.swift`, `AnalysisStore.swift`). `shots` is CJ-24 (256 px joint colour histogram), not VR-14/VR-S2's 64×36 luma. The sheet is CJ-27's 'Analyzing' sheet with Stop, not VR's 'Analysing Video' sheet with Cancel. Faces are CJ3/CJ-30 (10 Hz, 1280 px, mouth = inner-lip gap ÷ face height), but VR-60 uses outer-lip height and adds it 'behind a cache version bump of the subjects kind'. Identity linking (IoU ≥ 0.3, 1 s gap, restart at shots) is CJ-31, which VR-21 re-does in the core. The device rule is CJ-32 (Neural Engine pinned) against VR-S1 rule 3 (default, else CPU). The converted reader for log and HDR is CJ-23, which VR-S1 rule 4 decides again. The tool is CJ-25 `get_media_analysis` (source ticks, normalised 0…1 coordinates) against VR-17 `get_subjects` (clip time, pixels, VR-13). Planner proofs run on canned analyses (CJ-26) against VR2's live Vision on f1. **CJ-8 (c): 'Every analysis kind lives under cache/analysis/<kind>/; no bet adds a sibling folder', which VR-11's `cache/subjects/<id>.bin` breaks.** CJ-20 already decides 'never at import', which VR1's owner question re-asks. Lane C order (cj.md:532) says 'VR needs CJ2b's shot split, CJ3's faces and CJ5'.
objections.fix: Rebase VR on CJ2a, CJ2b, CJ3 and CJ5, and delete VR's duplicates: VR-10, VR-11, VR-12's signature, VR-14, VR-15, VR-S2, VR-S1 rules 2–4 and 6, MediaSubjects.swift, ShotSignature.swift and get_subjects. VR1 becomes 'two more kinds in CJ's store': `people` (`VNDetectHumanRectanglesRequest` r2) and `saliency` (attention r2), read through `get_media_analysis`, plus View ▸ Show Subjects. VR-S1 shrinks to people and saliency only, or folds into CJ-S2. Depends: VR1 ← CJ3 (and CJ2b for shots); VR3 ← CJ5. Restate VR-13 and VR-20's `subjects` in CJ-22's frame (normalised, display orientation, media source ticks). VR-21 keeps only what CJ-31 does not decide (scoring, hysteresis, face–person containment). VR6 reads CJ-30's mouth opening. VR2–VR4 proofs run on canned analyses (CJ-26), and Vision tolerances stay in CJ3 and VR1.

objections.where: VR-30, VR-37, VR3 Swift `ProjectDocument+VerticalCopy.swift`, VR3 proof row 9, VR3 'the File item, under Duplicate's group'
objections.claim: VR-30 copies through 'File ▸ Duplicate's path (the package with cache/, media/ and graphics/)' and says the copy shares the source's analysis. Neither part exists. Frame Job has no File ▸ Duplicate. An untitled document never reads a carried cache: it gets a fresh temporary cache folder.
objections.evidence: `AppDelegate+Menus.swift:119-193` has no Duplicate item; the only 'Duplicate' is Edit's clip duplicate (:214). cj.md:156 says the same: 'The File menu has Save As… and no project Duplicate'. `ProjectDocument.swift:761-770`: `intendedCacheDirectory` is `fileURL/cache` or, for an untitled document, a new `NSTemporaryDirectory()/FrameJob/<UUID>`, never `autosavedContentsFileURL/cache`. Only graphics/ is seeded from the autosave copy (`ProjectDocument+Graphics.swift:56-65`). So the copy re-runs thumbnails, peaks, speech and analysis, and proof row 9 ('a second run on the copy reuses the cache') fails. CJ-51 (CJ5) already defines a new untitled document seeded with the kept media's caches, analysis included.
objections.fix: Build the copy on CJ5's mechanism (CJ-51's new document with copied caches), or state an explicit seed of `temporaryCacheDirectory` from the source's `cache/` (APFS clone), with its proof row. Drop 'File ▸ Duplicate' from VR-30 and the menu placement, and correct VR-37's 'share' to 'copied into'.

objections.where: 'Actions' bullet 3 (vr.md:93-95); VR2 Core 'maps samples to clip time by `source_at`'; VR-17
objections.claim: `speed_map.rs:295 source_at(t)` is described as 'clip time to source time through speed, ramps and reverse'. It covers ramps only, and it answers source ticks read since `in` with no reversal.
objections.evidence: `SpeedMap::of` returns None for every clip that is not ramped (`speed_map.rs:212-227`), so a constant-speed clip has no map. `source_at` answers 'source ticks read by clip time t', relative to `in` (:293-305). Reversal is reflected by callers, e.g. `audio_duck_speech.rs:31-67` `speech_in_clip`, which handles the base rate, a SpeedMap and `reversed` (`d − b, d − a`). `Project::source_map` (`speed_segments.rs:243-273`) does not reflect reversal either.
objections.fix: Map through one shared helper shaped like `speech_in_clip`: `SpeedMap::of` else `/ speed`, reflected over `media.duration` when reversed. Better, extract it from `audio_duck_speech.rs` so the core has one implementation. Name it in VR2's Core bullet and cite it in place of `source_at`. VR-17's Swift side needs `ReverseMirror` beside `SourceMap`.

objections.where: VR2 phase (vr.md:577-650)
objections.claim: VR2 is too big for one litecode pipeline, the failure the brief says to split for now (AP2, AP8 and AP10 were split after the fact).
objections.evidence: One phase holds: a ≤400-line planner (association, scoring, hysteresis, composition, dead zone, cuts, loss, two people); a second ≤400-line module (coverage, composition into existing ends, gap scheduling, splits of existing actions, `replace`); the op with its strict reader and seven refusals; an `edit_background.rs` visibility change; two new `Kind`s plus `op_schema.rs` arms; `scope.rs`; two test files; a sheet, a command and an MCP handler that analyses first; VR-S3; 9 proof rows; 8 mutants.
objections.fix: Split it. VR2a: planner and `reframe_clip` on clips with no position actions (`subject`/`center`/`fit`/`keep`, cuts, loss, backdrop), the op tool, VR-S3. VR2b: composition into existing actions and `replace` (VR-27), then Clip ▸ Follow Subject and its sheet. Give each its own proof rows and mutants.

objections.where: VR-7 vs VR-20 `fit`, VR-25, VR-26, VR-29
objections.claim: VR-7 says the 'whole' treatment is 'always paired with a blurred backdrop', but VR-25 makes no copy without `backdrop`. VR-29 (Follow Subject, Where Empty: Show Whole) names no backdrop track. VR-26 allows `fit` and `center` on nest clips, but the backdrop builder refuses a nest.
objections.evidence: vr.md:220-224, :287-291, :295-296, :317-322. `edit_background.rs:355-380` refuses a nest clip for the blur. `fit` and `whole` are two spellings across `follow` and `where_empty` with no stated difference.
objections.fix: Define `fit` and `whole` once. Say VR-7's guarantee holds only when `backdrop` is given, or make the op add the track itself. Make Follow Subject pass one (or add a Backgrounds track as VR-34 does). Refuse or drop `fit` on a nest clip, or state that a nest shown whole shows the canvas.

objections.where: VR-7, VR-26, VR-33, VR2 proof row 2
objections.claim: `video.motion` is never mentioned. A preset moves and scales the drawn layer after the actions, so a followed clip with a During or edge motion breaks the no-canvas guarantee, and the magenta-corner proof would fail.
objections.evidence: `motion.rs:1-30`: presets produce scale factor F, rotation φ and offset Δ applied at `recipe.rs`'s `moved` on top of evaluated placement. `model_motion.rs:175-206` lists ZoomOut, Slide*, Spin, Pulse, Shake, Drift, Bounce.
objections.fix: Add a rule: a clip with a non-inert `video.motion` is `keep` and listed, or followed with its motion left on and VR-7 excluding the motion's span. Add a refusal sentence or a summary reason, and a proof row on a clip with a During motion.

objections.where: VR-33 (which clips are followed), VR-34
objections.claim: Existing backgrounds are misclassified. A 'Blurred Background' copy or an image plate spans the canvas, so it would be followed with `subject` (saliency on a blurred picture) while the step adds a second backdrop. A colour plate under `keep` shrinks by the smaller ratio and leaves the canvas showing.
objections.evidence: `edit_background.rs:1-18, 86-90`: both kinds sit on a new back-most track, sized or filled to the canvas, and the copy is named 'Blurred Background'. The `keep` rule is `edit_canvas.rs:60-90`'s scale × min ratio (0.5625 from 16:9 to 9:16).
objections.fix: Add a class to VR-33: an existing blurred copy is removed and replaced by the run's backdrop, or re-filled at fill scale; a plate is re-filled to the new canvas. Add both to the VR3 fixture and to the summary.

objections.where: VR-41 and VR4 Swift ('CaptionLayout.swift (581) takes nothing'); 'Read across: W-7 and W-10'
objections.claim: VR-41 changes the shipped subtitle cue builder, which lives in CaptionLayout.swift, so the file does take lines. The same H-based rule is written in two more places that would drift. The change alters Generate and Import Captions on every portrait project, not just Make Vertical, yet it is recorded as 'W-7 stands'.
objections.evidence: Size `height * preset.sizeFraction` at `CaptionLayout.swift:327` and y `preset.yFraction * height` at :363; the same at `TextPane.swift:453, 457` (Text ▸ Presets ▸ Caption) and `TranscribeSheetController+Style.swift:213` (the sheet's preview). objections.fix: Name the three sites, or route them through one function. Record VR-41 as an amendment to W-7 and §4.2's Caption preset, covering portrait projects in every caption door. Add the `captions.md` line, and pay the CaptionLayout toll first if the edit passes the cap.

objections.where: VR-43, VR4 proof rows 7-8, VR-E/JOB-35
objections.claim: VR-43 fixes the six bundled templates, but a project already holds its own copy of each template it inserted, under graphics/. The owner's trial projects, cut before VR4 lands, keep `ctx.height / 1080` and their lower thirds grow ×1.78 in the vertical version the trial judges. Proof row 7 also measures nothing: a raster made at 1080×1920 cannot have alpha outside its own frame.
objections.evidence: `graphic/tests/graphics/lower-third.js:20` `u = ctx.height / 1080`. app/CLAUDE.md: Insert ▸ Graphic writes the module into the package's `graphics/` (GraphicStore `write(name:source:)`). Row 7: 'keeps its alpha bounding box inside the frame'.
objections.fix: Have VR-42 detect a project module whose text equals an old bundled revision and offer, or apply, the new text, listing it in the summary. Otherwise state the limit and count such graphics. Replace row 7 with a measurable claim: no opaque pixel within N px of the frame edge, or each template's content bounding box at 9:16 equal to its 16:9 one scaled by u.

objections.where: VR-27 'A cut inside an existing action splits the action there: set_action shortens it and add_action carries its end and curve, as AU-80's ⌥ point does'
objections.claim: Shortening an action without rewriting its end changes what it animates: a volume ramp reaches its end early, and a zoom finishes early. AU-83 rewrites the first half's end to the evaluated value at t. An eased action cannot be split without re-easing both halves, and an action left past the clip's end cannot be split at all.
objections.evidence: AU-83 (`designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md`): 'the point dragged is A's new end, starting at the evaluated volume at t'; 'for an eased A … the shape between is re-eased on each side'; 'one a trim left running past the clip's end (add_action would refuse the split's second half)'.
objections.fix: Specify the split as edit_split.rs's narrowing: the first half's end is the full evaluated state at the cut, over every key the action names. State that an eased action is re-eased, which changes the audio and picture between keys, and count it in the summary. Say what happens to an action past the clip's end (no split, so the cut is carried approximately). Add a test that a split linear volume action plays unchanged.

objections.where: VR-36 `make_vertical_version`, VR-28 `reframe_clip`'s tool, VR-17 `get_subjects`
objections.claim: Each tool analyses before it answers and 'answers when it ends', with no bound. A long project's Vision pass runs for minutes, past an MCP client's call timeout. This is the reason `export` became asynchronous.
objections.evidence: Risks: 'A one-hour recording at 5 Hz takes minutes even windowed'. #326 (`export` answers an `export_id`; `export_status`). CJ-25: get_media_analysis 'waits with a bound, as get_transcript does'.
objections.fix: Give each tool CJ-25's bound and say what it answers past it: an 'analysing' answer naming the coverage, retried by the caller, or a job id with a status tool. Add a proof row using `-RCDevAnalysisHold`.

objections.where: VR1/VR2/VR3 Swift and Docs (the three menu items and the two sheets)
objections.claim: Three new menu items have no `perform_menu_item` allow-table and inventory rows, and the new sheets have no screen catalog entries. VR3's dev accept (`-RCDevVerticalAccept`) needs `perform_menu_item` on File ▸ Make Vertical Version… to work at all.
objections.evidence: `app/Sources/UIMenuTable.swift:1-14`: a menu item with no row is refused as `unclassified` and fails `v2_menu.py` H1/H2 against `tools/proof/capture_spike/inventory.json`. cj.md's CJ2b lists `UIMenuTable.swift` and `inventory.json` rows and 'a screen in designs/screens/ for the sheet'.
objections.fix: Per phase, add the `UIMenuTable.swift` verdict and `inventory.json` rows for View ▸ Show Subjects, Clip ▸ Follow Subject… and File ▸ Make Vertical Version…. Add `designs/screens/` entries for the Follow Subject and Make Vertical Version sheets, and root `CLAUDE.md`'s dev-default list entries for `-RCDevVerticalAccept` (and any hold default).

objections.where: VR6 Core 'reads the mic clips' media speech spans, which are already in the project'; VR-60
objections.claim: `media.speech` is not generally in the project. It is written only by `set_media_speech` when a Speech duck is set, so most media have no spans.
objections.evidence: AU-110: spans are 'written by the op set_media_speech'; app/CLAUDE.md DuckSpeech: 'Every duck edit of a Speech duck … puts ops before the set_audio'. The Silero VAD cache (`cache/speech/`) is where every media's speech lives.
objections.fix: Have VR6's command and tool put `DuckSpeech.ops` (the `set_media_speech` each mic media lacks) in the same grouped step before `reframe_clip`, as Duck by Speech does, and refuse by name a mic with no speech cache. Take mouth opening from CJ-30, not a new landmark pass.

objections.claim: The conditional linked-versions phase has four concrete errors and is too big for one pipeline: a colliding op name, an FFI claim that is false, a byte-equality proof that cannot hold, and a toll already paid.
objections.evidence: (1) `set_shape` already exists: the shape clip's patch, `edit_props.rs`'s five patches. (2) VR-74 'Each shape has its own composition plan', but `rc_project_composition_plan(const RcProject *p)` takes no options (`framejob_core.h:379`), so 'No new export' is wrong. (3) Proof 2 'byte for byte' fails wherever VR-27 approximated a move inside an existing action, where the copy differs from the exact F_v(t)∘placement(t). (4) 'ProjectSnapshot.swift … the audio group out to AudioProps.swift' was paid by audio AP11 (`AudioProps.swift:36,131` holds `DuckProps`, `AudioProps`); recipe.rs's hash cut is CJ0 T3. Also `Clip.shapes` and `tracks[].shape` sit beside the existing `Clip.shape` vocabulary.
objections.fix: Rename the concept (e.g. 'versions' or 'framings'), so the ops become add_version/set_version/remove_version. Name the FFI change: an options form of the plan export, or a shaped view as `rc_project_scoped` is. Restrict proof 2 to fixtures with no approximated moves, or state its tolerance. Fix the tolls. Pre-split VR7 into model, ops and carries (VR7a) and recipe, plan and export (VR7b).

objections.claim: `speed_map.rs:295 source_at(t)` is described as 'clip time to source time through speed, ramps and reverse'. It covers ramps only, and it answers source ticks read since `in` with no reversal.

Reversal is reflected by callers, e.g. `audio_duck_speech.rs:31-67` `speech_in_clip`, which handles the base rate, a SpeedMap and `reversed` (`d − b, d − a`). `Project::source_map` (`speed_segments.rs:243-273`) does not reflect reversal either.

objections.where: VR-27 'A cut inside an existing action splits the action there: set_action shortens it and add_action carries its end and curve, as AU-80's ⌥ point does'
objections.claim: Shortening an action without rewriting its end changes what it animates: a volume ramp reaches its end early, and a zoom finishes early. AU-83 rewrites the first half's end to the evaluated value at t. An eased action cannot be split without re-easing both halves, and an action left past the clip's end cannot be split at all.
objections.evidence: AU-83 (`designs/spec/11-decisions/audio.md`): 'the point dragged is A's new end, starting at the evaluated volume at t'; 'for an eased A … the shape between is re-eased on each side'; 'one a trim left running past the clip's end (add_action would refuse the split's second half)'.
objections.fix: Specify the split as edit_split.rs's narrowing: the first half's end is the full evaluated state at the cut, over every key the action names. State that an eased action is re-eased, which changes the audio and picture between keys, and count it in the summary. Say what happens to an action past the clip's end (no split, so the cut is carried approximately). Add a test that a split linear volume action plays unchanged.
